history.contentIn: The Stratospheric Controlled Perturbation Experiment (SCoPEx) was a scientific initiative led by Harvard University, aimed at investigating the behavior of aerosol particles in the stratosphere. Principal investigator Frank Keutsch and his team, including David Keith, presented the concept at various forums, such as the American Geophysical Union Fall Meeting in 2017. Importantly, SCoPEx was designed solely to enhance computer models assessing the risks and benefits of solar geoengineering, not to deploy geoengineering techniques or directly cool the planet. The experiment proposed using a scientific balloon gondola to release a very small quantity of calcium carbonate—ranging from 100 grams to 2 kilograms—into a controlled volume of approximately 1 km long and 100 meters in diameter. A 2021 hardware test in Sweden, conducted in collaboration with the Swedish Space Corporation, was limited to testing the platform and did not involve particle release. Following recommendations for societal engagement, Harvard announced in March 2024 that Keutsch would not continue with SCoPEx, and the platform will be repurposed for unrelated stratospheric research.
